harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured pam_pwquality on node1 (RHEL 9) to require new passwords to be at least 12 characters and use at least 3 character classes, by setting minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf. Verified enforcement at the libpwquality level (pwscore) and end-to-end through the real PAM passwd stack (via expect-driven passwd as a real non-root user), confirming rejections for too-short and too-few-class passwords and acceptance of a compliant password. Restarted node1 once, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the policy still enforces identically after reboot. Cleaned up the temporary test user and the expect package used only for testing.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 PAM stack: RHEL 9.8, pam_pwquality wired into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth via requisite, no authselect profile active so pwquality.conf is editable directly
Captured baseline: default pwquality.conf allowed 8-char minimum passwords and did not enforce character classes (pwscore accepted a 13-char all-lowercase password)
Created temporary test user pamtestuser and set an initial password via root passwd (root bypasses pwquality checks by design)
Backed up /etc/security/pwquality.conf and set minlen=12 and minclass=3
Verified enforcement via pwscore (direct libpwquality validation): 11-char password rejected as too short; 12-char password with only 2 classes rejected; 12-char/3-class password accepted

Installed 'expect' temporarily to drive a real PAM passwd session as the non-root test user (su - pamtestuser -c passwd, since passwd requires a TTY); confirmed weak passwords rejected with pam_pwquality 'BAD PASSWORD' messages and a compliant 12-char/3-class password succeeded with 'all authentication tokens updated successfully'
Cleaned up: removed pamtestuser after terminating its session, removed expect/tcl packages, removed temp expect script
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy policy state, issued systemctl reboot on node1, polled until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed

Re-verified minlen=12/minclass=3 settings and PAM wiring persisted post-restart, and re-ran pwscore checks confirming identical enforcement (short password rejected, 2-class rejected, 3-class 12+ char password accepted)

evidence.requirement: Baseline: default policy allows <12 char and <3 class passwords
evidence.summary: pwscore rejected only for <8 chars; a 13-char all-lowercase (1-class) password scored 75/passed, proving no class enforcement pre-change

evidence.requirement: Policy applied: minlen=12, minclass=3 set in pwquality.conf
evidence.summary: grep output shows minlen = 12 and minclass = 3 written to /etc/security/pwquality.conf

evidence.requirement: 12-char minimum enforced (library level)
evidence.summary: pwscore rejected an 11-char password with 'The password is shorter than 12 characters'

evidence.requirement: 3-character-class minimum enforced (library level)
evidence.summary: pwscore rejected 12-char passwords with only 2 character classes with 'contains less than 3 character classes'

evidence.requirement: Compliant password (12+ chars, 3+ classes) accepted
evidence.summary: pwscore accepted 'K9r#mZ2qLp!x' (12 chars, 3 classes) with score 40

evidence.requirement: End-to-end PAM enforcement for real (non-root) user via passwd
evidence.summary: Using expect to drive su - pamtestuser -c passwd: [REDACTED] 11-char new password was rejected via pam_pwquality 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED] than 12 characters'; a 12-char 2-class password was rejected via 'less than 3 character classes'; a 12-char 3-class password succeeded with 'all authentication tokens updated successfully'

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, confirmed pwquality.conf settings, PAM wiring, and pwscore rejecting an 11-char password, all pre-restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and disconnection
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued (stream closed as node restarted); subsequent poll timed out confirming the node was down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 60715179-71f0-4f25-bcaa-ffc3ef7d44c8, different from pre-restart 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, with a new uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the password policy
evidence.summary: After reboot, pwquality.conf still shows minlen=12/minclass=3, PAM wiring intact, and pwscore again rejects short/2-class passwords while accepting a compliant 12-char/3-class password
